jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Strategy - Global Banking & Markets
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 273705

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Purpose

The Scotiabank Strategy group is a central team focused on shaping the Bank’s strategic agenda, considering both enterprise-wide and business / function-specific strategic questions and opportunities.

Reporting to the Vice President, Enterprise Strategy, the Director, Enterprise Strategy is a key representative for GBM at the Enterprise Strategy level. GBM encompasses Corporate and Investment Banking and Global Markets, offering clients a range of financial services including lending, transaction services, investment banking advice, and access to capital markets. The Director plays a critical role in supporting the contextualization of GBM strategy within the context of the Bank’s overall strategic framework.  The Director also works closely with GBM leadership, Enterprise Strategy partners, and Corporate Functions to deliver strategic insights and, support strategic planning and execution as needed across GBM. The role focuses on shaping strategic direction, translating strategic direction into actionable initiatives, providing analytical rigor, and ensuring strategies are practical, measurable, and executable.

The incumbent combines strong strategy development capabilities and experience in a top-tier strategy consulting or corporate strategy environment with either experience in Corporate & Investment Banking, Capital Markets, and/or related businesses, or a demonstrated ability to rapidly build domain expertise in complex industries. The successful candidate will be expected to quickly develop a deep understanding of GBM businesses, products, clients, and market dynamics and engage credibly with senior business leaders on strategic priorities.

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will be involved in:

Strategy Development & Planning Support

•    Support the development and refresh of GBM strategy in alignment with the Bank’s enterprise strategy, helping to “connect the dots” across business lines and corporate functions.
•    Lead discrete strategic workstreams and targeted deep dives across GBM strategic priorities, including growth, profitability, client experience, and operating model initiatives.
•    Identify, assess, and evaluate strategic opportunities and issues specific to GBM, including implications of market trends, competitive dynamics, regulatory developments, and emerging risks.
•    Support the annual GBM strategic planning process, including preparation of analysis and materials for Executive Management and the Board, ensuring alignment with enterprise processes and requirements.
•    Provide structured analytical support and strategic recommendations to senior leaders, under the guidance of the VP.

Strategy Execution, Monitoring & Insights

•    Design and oversee execution roadmaps for GBM strategic initiatives, working closely with cross-functional partners to ensure alignment, momentum, and delivery against milestones.
•    Design strategic KPIs and tracking mechanisms to monitor progress against GBM strategic objectives.
•    Conduct benchmarking and competitive analysis against local and global peers to identify performance gaps, opportunities, and emerging best practices.
•    Monitor execution risks, dependencies, and trade-offs, and escalate issues with clear options and recommendations.
•    Support periodic assessments of GBM’s strategic positioning, operating model, and performance outcomes.

Thought Leadership & Strategic Advisory

•    Act as a thought partner to GBM and enterprise leaders by providing effective challenge, fresh perspectives, and fact-based insights on strategic priorities and must win initiatives.

•    Facilitate strategic discussions with business leaders, challenge assumptions where appropriate, and drive alignment on priorities and investment decisions.
•    Synthesize complex analysis into clear, compelling stories and recommendations tailored to executive audiences.
•    Operate as a strategy advisor to GBM leadership, applying a structured problem solving approach, hypothesis-driven analysis, and executive-level communication to complex business challenges.
•    Contribute to the preparation and facilitation of GBM and enterprise strategy offsites, planning sessions, and leadership workshops.
•    Stay current on global capital markets, investment banking trends, and broader financial services developments to inform strategic thinking.

Stakeholder Management & Collaboration

•    Establish credibility with senior GBM executives by combining structured problem solving, data-driven analysis, commercial insight, and an understanding of client, market, and competitive dynamics.
•    Build strong working relationships with GBM leadership, enterprise strategy colleagues, and partners across finance, risk, technology, and other corporate functions.
•    Bridge silos and enable alignment across teams to support execution of GBM priorities.
•    Act as a trusted partner to senior executives, helping them clarify priorities and translate strategy into execution.

Team Leadership, Culture & Risk

•    Lead and mentor junior strategy resources and contribute to building a high-performing, inclusive strategy team.
•    Support talent development through coaching, feedback, and knowledge sharing.
•    Perform all activities in accordance with the Bank’s risk culture, risk appetite, and control environment.
•    Ensure strategy work incorporates appropriate consideration of financial, operational, regulatory, and conduct risks.
•    Foster a customer-focused mindset by embedding client impact and outcomes into strategic analysis and recommendations.

Dimensions

•    Leads multiple complex strategy workstreams with cross-functional teams across GBM and the broader Bank.
•    Exercises independent judgment within defined scope on high impact initiatives; escalates key decisions and trade-offs appropriately.
•    Regular interaction with senior leaders (SVPs, EVPs) within GBM and enterprise functions, with less frequent direct exposure to Group Heads and Board-level forums.
•    Operates in a highly collaborative environment requiring strong influencing skills without direct authority.

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed? We’d love to work with you if you have the following:

•    University degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related discipline; MBA or equivalent post graduate degree strongly preferred.
•    Typically 7–12 years of relevant experience, including strategy roles within financial services and/or top-tier management consulting.
•    Solid working knowledge of Global Banking and Markets, Capital Markets, and Investment Banking businesses and products.
•    Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional strategy or transformation initiatives

•    Exceptional structured problem-solving, critical thinking, and quantitative analytical capabilities

•    Ability to synthesize complex information into clear, compelling recommendations for executive audiences.
•    Proven ability to communicate complex ideas clearly and concisely to senior audiences.Demonstrated success building credibility quickly with senior business leaders and navigating highly matrixed organizations.
•    Collaborative leadership style with experience developing high potential talent.
•    Strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills.
•    Proficiency in MS Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
•    Proficiency in French and/or Spanish is an asset.

Successful candidates will play a key role in leading enterprise and business line strategic projects, managing relationships with senior management and stakeholders at all levels throughout the Bank and driving the Bank’s strategic planning process.

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will be involved in:

- High-touch support; where the team will be driving strategy development in specific areas / businesses

- Low-touch support; where the team will be providing advisory services, e.g., participating at the steering committees for key initiatives, engaging in specific workstreams of the project

- Complete competitive / business environment research and benchmarking to determine emerging issues and trends and analyze the impact / implications of those trends on the Bank's strategic plan

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed? We’d love to work with you if you have the following:

- 2+ years post-MBA or 5+ years post-undergraduate experience in consulting, corporate strategy / development, or investment banking

- Ability to deliver results in a fast-paced, challenging and dynamic business environment

- Proven strong sales and closing skills

- Very strong networking ability

- Very strong negotiation skills

- Strong relationship management skills

The incumbent understands the Canadian Business Banking objectives, and has a thorough knowledge of segment, strategies and structure, as well as its lending and deposit products and services

Scotiabank’s Corporate Finance Advisory team sits at the intersection of banking and capital markets. Our team advises corporate clients on capital structure, financing strategy, and credit positioning, as well as strategic decisions across valuation, M&A, shareholder dynamics, and thematic market and sector trends.

We partner across the full GBM platform to deliver analytically driven recommendations and differentiated insights that create value for our clients. - Support deal sourcing and execution through rigorous fundamental analysis, capital markets insights, scenario modeling, and client-ready presentation materials

- You have an undergraduate or graduate Degree in Business, Finance, Science, Technology, Engineering, Economics or Mathematics discipline or related fields to be completed between December 2026 and July 2027

Derivatives), Commodity Derivatives, Prime / CMF, DCM (inc. MCM / Structured Credit / Securitization), and CIB (inc. ECM / LevFin).

Participate in industry groups and trade associations and work with colleagues across the US and international jurisdictions to drive a consistent and collaborative approach to compliance.

Programme Overview:

Scotiabank offers an outstanding opportunity for students to gain real hands-on experience through our Global Capital Markets Summer Internship programme commencing in June 2027.

This 10-week programme is designed for students in their penultimate year of study who are eager to learn and have a passion for financial markets.

Capital Markets spans a number of predominantly client facing business functions, and as such, we encourage applications from broad array of disciplines. From risk taking trading roles, to client relationship management (typically known as ‘Sales’ or ‘DCM’ functions), and from developed to emerging markets, Scotiabank’s rotational-style programme offers a truly exceptional foundational experience for any candidate with a keen interest in markets.

As an intern, you will gain exceptional insights into the daily workings of several specific Capital Markets desks including:

- CMF: Collateral Management & Funding

- Debt Capital Markets

- Emerging Markets Relationship Management/Sales

- FX Relationship Management/Sales & Trading

- Global Equity Sales & Trading

- Global Fixed Income Relationship Management/Sales & Trading

- Prime Services

What You Can Expect:

During the programme, you will:

- Shadow traders to learn risk management techniques, and develop key trading/market making skills in a live market environment

- Be immersed in real-world business development and client acquisition experiences, offering a firm grounding in  a truly global client base  spanning; official institutions, bank treasury desks, global asset managers, pension funds and alternative asset managers

- Interact with stakeholders to develop a strong understanding of the global markets and products, with the opportunity to apply knowledge to real world situations

- Complete a variety of key business-line projects which includes preparing market commentary, analysing client trading data, and other ad hoc tasks

- Develop an understanding of Scotiabank’s products, services, risk appetite and risk culture

- Deliver a final presentation to leaders within Capital Markets

Our internship is designed to give you real insight into life at Scotiabank. Alongside your day-to-day responsibilities, you’ll take part in:

- A weekly speaker series with leaders from across the Bank

- Peer to peer intern presentations

- Social and networking events

- A CSR project that supports one of our charity partners

Upon completion of the internship, exceptional interns will be considered for entry onto our 2028 Global Capital Markets Rotational Graduate Programme where they will rotate across several desks with the goal of obtaining a permanent position within Global Banking and Markets.

- You are a penultimate year undergraduate university student graduating in summer 2028

jobs.title: Client Relationship Manager, Commercial Agriculture Banking - Lethbridge
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 271513

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Client Relationship Manager, Commercial Agriculture Banking - Lethbridge, Alberta

The Client Relationship Manager (CRM) is a product generalist who possesses a good understanding of financial products and services and focuses on the cross sell and retention of existing commercial customers. You are responsible for identifying prospects in target markets, developing proposed sales pipelines, conducting prospect sales calls and qualifying opportunities based on customer information and a high level of due diligence.

The Client Relationship Manager (CRM) is responsible for ensuring effective relationship management and conducts sales planning and fulfills the execution of service for existing customer base. The incumbent is also responsible for analysis and completion of credit applications.

This role contributes to the overall success of the Canadian Agriculture Banking team in Commercial Banking ensuring specific individual goals, plans and initiatives are executed/delivered in support of the team’s business strategies and objectives.  Ensures all activities conducted in compliance with governing regulations, internal policies and procedures.

Accountabilities:

Champions a client-driven culture to deepen client relationships and leverage broader Bank relationships, systems and knowledge.

Promotes the development and profitable growth of the Canadian Business Banking portfolio in the assigned market area by:

-

- Developing and implementing a marketing strategy to maximize business development opportunities for sustainable growth.

- Developing sales plans for prospects and existing customers.

- Identifying prospects/referrals from other internal/external networks.

- Analyzing prospect lists and prioritizing business development opportunities based on market data and customer analytics.

- Partner with internal resources for non-credit related products.

- Referring customers and prospects to the appropriate Canadian Business Banking segment and partners as appropriate.

Pursues a business development program within the assigned market area according to agreed-upon growth objectives by:

-

- Direct selling of credit and non-credit commercial products to prospects and customers.

- Maintaining an appropriate ongoing sales pipeline and calling program.

- Identifying and facilitating the involvement of key Bank resources and stakeholders to further business interests.

- Maintaining effective follow-up with prospects/referrals on any unsuccessful opportunities.

- Updating client or contact information accurately and in a timely fashion.

Builds and maintains a market profile in the assigned market area with both internal and external contacts by;

-

- Planning and completing relationship activities that generate sales opportunities and/or provide value to clients.

- Building and maintaining an awareness of local market and general economic conditions.

- Meeting with business leaders and other centres of influence.

- Participating in local professional and community events and associations to develop and expand network of contacts.

- Liaising and utilizing Bank product specialists to stay abreast of new enhancements, products and services, and to fulfil identified client needs.

Ensures all aspects of assigned relationships receive ongoing attention, as required to maintain, improve, grow and retain the relationship by.

Manage an assigned credit portfolio for authorizations up to $25MM at an acceptable level of risk by:

-

- Completing credit reviews in a timely and sufficiently detailed fashion.

- Authorizing, renewing or declining customer requests within standard Bank policies and authorized limits, forwarding others as per established processes.

- Preparing and/or ensuring all documentation is properly prepared.

- Ensuring accounts adhere to the conditions of authorization.

- Identifying and resolving deviations from the conditions of authorization.

- Ensuring early identification of problem loans and ensuring the accuracy of risk ratings through identification of changes in account quality via review of industry/economic trends.

- Making recommendations relative to structure, monitoring and risk rating to Global Risk Management as issues are identified.  This may include exiting a relationship.

Ensures satisfactory onboarding of clients by:

-

- Completing diligence to ensure through understanding of the Client’s business and expected business activity and that it aligns with the Bank’s risk tolerance.

Champion sustainment of the Operating Model by:

-

- Taking ownership that activities and behaviours align to roles and responsibilities and adherence to guidelines and processes within the Team.

Champion and support a culture of diversity and other initiatives aligned with the Bank strategy.

Understand how the Bank’s risk appetite and risk culture should be considered in day-to-day activities and decisions.

Actively pursues effective and efficient operations of his/her respective areas, while ensuring the adequacy, adherence to and effectiveness of day-to-day business controls to meet obligations with respect to operational risk, regulatory compliance risk, AML/ATF risk and conduct risk, including but not limited to responsibilities under the Operational Risk Management Framework, Regulatory Compliance Risk Management Framework, AML/ATF Global Handbook and the Guidelines for Business Conduct.

Champions a high-performance environment and contributes to an inclusive work environment.

Dimensions:

-

- Strong organizational skills are necessary to manage significant data from multiple sources and balance various tasks from client service administration to borrower reporting processing to credit related support.

- The incumbent will interact primarily with various internal partners which include: Global Risk Management, the Business Service Center, Enhanced Due Diligence Unit CRA, Small Business, Retail, Wealth Management, Global Banking and Markets, Cash Management Contact Centre, Payments and Cash Management and could include other partners as well as the Canadian Business Banking Executive Office.

- The incumbent will also interact with external parties such as Solicitors, Accountants, Professional Service Providers and possibly External Bank Groups.

- The incumbent continually works with clients providing service consistent with Scotia Service Standards, Complaint Resolution Standards and Procedures. The CRM looks for opportunities to promote the sale of bank product and services.

- The environment is fast paced and demanding and will at times require priorities be re-adjusted to accommodate urgent requests.

Education / Experience / Other Information:

Education

-

- Undergraduate degree in business or economics or work equivalency.

- Other training requirements as determined by the Bank from time to time.

Skills/Work Experience

- Previous work experience of at least three to four years, within Agriculture banking.

- Strong sales/closing skills.

- Strong communication and interpersonal skills and knowledge of Bank’s commercial lending and deposit products and services.

- Ability to conduct due diligence on the strength of customer financials for deals of lower to moderate complexity.

- Strong commercial credit.

- Incumbent requires a thorough knowledge of the commercial banking marketplace in Canada and general knowledge of the assigned market areas.

- Strong networking ability and negotiation skills.

Working Conditions:

- Work in a standard office-based environment; non-standard hours are a common occurrence.

- Travel within the assigned territory is required as well as a vehicle.

Whether you are a licensed Portfolio Manager, an emerging Associate Portfolio Manager, or a relationship focused Wealth Manager committed towards becoming registered as an APM then PM, we welcome exceptional candidates who are passionate about serving high-net- worth (HNW) and ultra-high-net-worth (UHNW) clients.

The scope of discretionary authority and portfolio management responsibility varies by licensing level and registration with provincial securities regulators, but ownership of client relationships and business development expectations apply across all roles .

Candidates will be assessed for the role that best aligns with their experience, licensing, and career trajectory.

Core Responsibilities Shared Across All Roles

Business Development & Growth

- Acquire new HNW and UHNW clients through proactive prospecting, referrals, networking, and centres of influence.

- Develop and execute client‑acquisition strategies aligned with market opportunities and business objectives.

- Maintain a disciplined and well‑documented prospect pipeline to support sustainable, profitable growth.

- Identify opportunities to consolidate assets, deepen client relationships, and increase share of wallet across the client lifecycle .

Client Relationship Management & Advice

- Develop deep, long-term client relationships through ongoing life based discovery.

- Gain an intimate understanding of clients’ goals, circumstances, values, and evolving wealth needs.

- Deliver holistic wealth advice that integrates investments, planning, tax, insurance, and banking solutions.

- Proactively identify gaps, risks, and opportunities to enhance client outcomes and experience.

- Act as the central relationship owner and trusted advisor for clients.

- Represent SJF internally and externally with professionalism, credibility, and a strong growth mindset.

Risk, Compliance & Professional Standards

- Ensure complete, accurate, and up to date KYC/IPQ documentation.

- Maintain ongoing suitability of strategies and recommendations as client circumstances evolve.

- Operate with strict adherence with regulatory requirements, internal policies, and conduct standards.

- Uphold SJF’s values of integrity, professionalism, and client first decision making.

Team & Culture

- Collaborate closely with the CRIA team who supports APM and PM development and other Total Wealth partners to deliver integrated solutions.

- Contribute to a high-performance, inclusive, and growth oriented team culture.

- Share knowledge, support team initiatives, and participate actively in meetings and development activities.

Who This Role Is For

Experienced discretionary investment professionals who are fully AR licensed with the provincial securities regulator to manage portfolios and deliver sophisticated investment counselling.

What You Bring

- CFA charter holder or CIM designation required.

- Must meet all regulatory requirements for Portfolio Manager registration (AR with the Ontario Securities Commission for example)

- Minimum 5+ years of discretionary portfolio management experience.

- Post‑secondary degree in Finance, Business, Economics, or related field.

2. Associate Portfolio Manager – SJF (AAR Registered, Development Toward Full PM Licensing) – L7

Who This Role Is For

Professionals who are AAR licensed with the provincial securities regulator and on the pathway to Portfolio Manager registration possessing strong investment knowledge and want to grow within SJF’s Total Wealth environment.

What You Bring

- CIM or CFA Level 1 required per regulatory requirements.

- Must meet all regulatory requirements for Associate Portfolio Manager registration (AAR with the Ontario Securities Commission for example)

- Interest in pursuing CFA, CFP, and/or LLQP is an asset.

- Strong investment literacy and ability to explain concepts clearly.

- Desire to develop into a full discretionary Portfolio Manager role.

- Strong client relationship and communication skills.

- Post‑secondary degree in Finance, Business, Economics, or related field.

3. Wealth Manager – SJF (Non-Registrant Relationship Lead) – L8

Who This Role Is For

Professionals who lead client relationships by collaborating closely with SJF’s Total Wealth and CRIA teams, without holding discretionary registration. We provide the training and support and opportunity to gain the experience required to become AAR registered and become an Associate Portfolio Manager title.

What You Bring

- CSC required; CIM preferred (must be completed within 24 months).

- Interest in pursuing CFA, CFP, and/or LLQP is an asset.

- Effective communication, relationship management, and business development skills.

- Business development and client relationship experience in an adjacent occupation (i.e., commercial banking, retail wealth management, mutual funds and insurance sales, accounting and tax planning for wealth management clients, trust or legal backgrounds, experience working with retail and wealth management clients and partners, etc.)

- Experience with HNW clients or wealth concepts is an asset.

- Post‑secondary education in Finance/Business or related fields.

WHAT ALL ROLES SHARE

SJF is looking for professionals who:

- Demonstrate integrity, trustworthiness, and sound judgment.

- Deliver best in class client experiences.

- Thrive in a collaborative, team-based wealth environment.

- Communicate clearly and credibly to sophisticated clients.

- Are motivated to learn, grow, and contribute to SJF’s Total Wealth mission.

WHATS IN IT FOR YOU

- Access to industry leading training, mentorship, and development.

- A multi‑disciplinary expert ecosystem supporting your success.

- Meaningful career pathways, including progression to registrant roles.

- A culture built on respect, collaboration, and client excellence.

Requisition ID: 273942

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Investment Associate provides advanced trading and client service support to Scotia iTRADE’s High Value and highly active trader client segment. This role requires specialized expertise in equity and derivatives markets, including the execution and management of single‑and multi‑legged options strategies, and the ability to apply complex risk, margin, and regulatory considerations in real time.

The incumbent engages with clients on high‑complexity inquiries and transactions, often involving significant financial exposure and time‑sensitive decision‑making. This requires a deep understanding of options pricing, volatility, margin requirements, and risk/reward profiles, as well as the ability to clearly explain advanced trading concepts to sophisticated investors.

The Investment Associate operates with a high degree of autonomy and professional judgment, resolving complex issues, supporting advanced order entry, and partnering closely with Credit, Compliance, and Order Management to mitigate firm and client risk. The role plays a critical part in maintaining operational integrity, risk controls, and client confidence, while also identifying opportunities to grow client assets and deepen relationships.

Major Accountabilities:

- Providing industry leading client experiences by:

- Answering advanced client service and trade related inquiries in a fast-paced technology-based environment and communicating advanced concepts clearly and effectively

- Liaising and collaborating with Management and colleagues to identify issues/trends, recommending solutions and executing solutions effectively

- Ensuring timely and prompt submission of client instructions and customer follow-up

- From time to time, leading or assisting with monitoring of customer communications of all types

- Adhering to and ensuring compliance with Know Your Customer requirements

- Acting quickly to alleviate errors and reduce firm exposure

- Reviewing approved order and status orders to appropriate exchanges and vendors

- Corresponding with clients and resolving client escalations via telephone on an advanced level

- Contribute to the effective functioning of SiT by:

- Building effective working relationships across the team and with various business lines and corporate functions

- Excellent written and oral communication skills to communicate highly technical concepts clearly and effectively to clients and internal stakeholders

jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 268855

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Funds Risk Management is responsible for risk management and analysis of Hedge Funds, Pensions Funds, Private Equity and other Investment Funds. As a Manager, you will be a key member of the Funds Risk Management team who is responsible for credit risk adjudication and ongoing monitoring of the financial health of the Hedge Funds portfolio. The team participates in customer due diligence meetings as well as monitoring and reporting for the assigned portfolio of accounts. The team works closely with three major Global Banking and Market’s (GBM) business lines - Prime Services, Collateral Management and Funding, and Credit Total Return Swaps to provide products and services to their hedge fund customers. You are expected to act as a strategic partner and trusted advisor to the GBM business lines with respect to risk related matters concerning Hedge Funds globally. You are expected to have a strong background of credit, market and counterparty credit risk management frameworks, related policies of the Bank, and industry best practices with regards to counterparty credit risk management.

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will:

- Approve, maintain and manage credit exposure to Hedge Funds clients across derivatives and secured financing transactions.

- Conduct proactive risk management of the Bank’s Hedge Funds Portfolio for assigned accounts by assessing clients’ portfolio risk, liquidity of client positions, credit limits and risk appetite ratios.

- Partner with our banking, business line and market risk colleagues to ensure that both credit and market risks are effectively evaluated and mitigated.

- Participate in Hedge Fund client due diligence calls/meetings and maintain the relationship to ensure appropriate ongoing monitoring of the portfolio.

- Conduct Credit and Market risk analysis of business requests, ensuring material issues are identified through concise commentary, and provide appropriate recommendations. This includes:

(i) comprehensive credit evaluation of counterparties to assess and mitigate investment, business and/or operational risk,

(ii) evaluate appropriateness of risk/return metrics of deal proposals, and

(iii) appropriateness of terms and conditions, exposures, margining, termination events and other covenants for a wide range of facilities including prime brokerage, repo/rev repos, foreign exchange, interest rate derivatives, and credit total return swaps.

- Assist and participate in the presentation of credits to Senior Management and the Senior Credit Committee

- Conduct ongoing monitoring of the credit quality of the portfolio and compile weekly early warnings reports for higher risk clients.

- Monitoring of deal terms and conditions carried out by other groups within the Bank and ensure limit overruns are regularized in a timely manner.

- Prepare portfolio reporting, documentation of processes and contribute to development and enhancement of processes and reporting requirements.

- Work with technology team to develop and enhance data analytics for senior management on the overall hedge fund portfolio as well as individual counterparties.

- Assist with preparation of the annual Hedge Funds Industry Report, and with assigned projects as required.

- Continuously develop and maintain a high degree of industry knowledge/expertise.

- Contribute to the department's goals and objectives through active participation in projects and initiatives.

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed? We’d love to work with you if you have:

- 3+ years institutional counterparty credit experience in a large financial institution.

- Experience in the analysis and risk management of Hedge Funds and/or other investment vehicles

- Solid knowledge of Secured Financing Transactions and derivatives.

- Market Risk experience is highly preferred.

- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, both written and oral.

- Strong time management, planning and organizing skills to manage multiple priorities.

- Ability to work in a fast-paced environment.

- MBA / CFA Charter qualifications are preferred, but not a prerequisite.

- Previous Credit Risk or Banking experience required.

- What’s in it for you?

- An inclusive & collaborative working environment that encourages creativity, curiosity, and celebrates success!

- We offer a competitive rewards package: Performance bonus, Employee Share Ownership Program, and Pension Plan Matching, Health Benefits from day one!

- Your career matters! You will have access to career development and progression opportunities.

jobs.title: Director Risk Run and Analytics
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 269904

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Role

The Director, Market Risk and Counterparty Credit Risk Run and Analytics, will lead the technology teams responsible for production support, analytics platforms, and critical risk calculation systems supporting Market Risk and Counterparty Credit Risk.

This role is accountable for ensuring stability, reliability, and effective delivery across three core areas:

-

- Run and Production Support

- Analytics Platforms

- VaR and Stress Testing Systems

The successful candidate will bring strong Capital Markets Risk knowledge, deep technology leadership experience, and the ability to influence both internal teams and senior stakeholders to build a stable, scalable, and future-proof technical environment. The use of AI, automation, and modern engineering practices is becoming a core expectation for this role.

What will we expect from you?

Run and Production Support

- Lead the enhanced support team responsible for day-to-day production stability across Market Risk and Counterparty Credit Risk applications.

- Partner closely with Risk Officers, Trading users, Front Office stakeholders, and Technology teams to resolve issues quickly and reduce recurring production riskAct as the technology gatekeeper to production, ensuring changes, releases, configurations, and deployments follow appropriate testing, controls, release management, and risk review processes.

- Maintain strong oversight of production health, including incident management, SLA performance, stability metrics, resiliency, and operational risk reduction.

- Ensure high availability, integrity, and reliability of critical risk systems and business processes.

- Drive continuous improvement in support practices, monitoring, automation, incident prevention, and root cause remediation.

Analytics Platforms

- Lead the analytics technology team supporting capital calculation, business intelligence, reporting, and analytics capabilities for Market Risk and Counterparty Credit Risk.

- Oversee platforms and capabilities including LMS(Limit Management System), Tableau, Power BI, and FRTB Aggregation.

- Ensure analytics solutions are stable, scalable, well-controlled, and aligned with business needs.

- Partner with stakeholders to define priorities, manage delivery, and improve the usability, quality, and reliability of analytics outputs.

- Drive modernization of analytics platforms, including automation, self-service reporting, data quality improvements, and adoption of AI-enabled capabilities where appropriate.

- Rationalize applications by migrating to enterprise approved targets and manage the application hygiene such as end of life, vulnerabilities and cyber security aspects, and reducing manual work for app hygiene with AI-enabled capabilities.

VaR and Stress Testing Systems

- Lead the technology team responsible for the critical VaR platform that produces VaR (Value at Risk), Stress Testing and PFE (Potential Future Exposure) outputs.

- Ensure the VaR and Stress Testing platforms meet expectations for accuracy, timeliness, resiliency, auditability, and regulatory readiness.

- Oversee operation support, enhancements, controls, and modernization of the VaR technology stack.

- Partner with Market Risk, CCR (Counterparty Credit Risk), Model Risk, Quants, Infrastructure, and Engineering teams to strengthen the platform and reduce operational risk.

- Ensure the platform can support evolving business, regulatory, and risk management requirements.

Strategic Leadership

- Influence the technology strategy for Market Risk and Counterparty Credit Risk by working with the team, stakeholders, and peer technology leaders to define a future-proof architecture.

- Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to challenge, escalate, and drive upstream teams to resolve recurring production, data, and process issues at their source.

- Build and execute a roadmap that improves system stability, scalability, resiliency, controls, and engineering efficiency.

- Promote AI, automation, and modern engineering practices to reduce manual effort, improve production support, and accelerate delivery.

- Provide technical direction and challenge existing practices where needed to improve long-term platform health.

- Negotiate priorities, timelines, risks, dependencies, and trade-offs with business and technology stakeholders.

- Communicate clearly with senior leadership on production risk, delivery status, strategic priorities, and investment needs.

People Leadership

- Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team of technology professionals across support, analytics, and risk systems delivery.

- Ensure the team has the right structure, skills, procedures, and governance to support critical risk platforms.

- Foster a culture of ownership, accountability, engineering excellence, continuous improvement, and production discipline.

- Develop talent, support succession planning, and create opportunities for team members to grow.

- Promote collaboration across Technology, Risk, Front Office, Infrastructure, Data, and Engineering teams.

What You Will Bring to Succeed

- Minimum 10 years of experience in Risk Technology, Capital Markets Technology, or a related technology leadership role.

- Strong knowledge of Capital Markets Risk, including Market Risk, Counterparty Credit Risk, VaR, Stress Testing, FRTB, risk monitoring, capital requirements, and regulatory expectations.

- Proven experience leading teams responsible for production support, technology delivery, and complex risk platforms.

- Experience supporting business-critical systems used by Market Risk, Credit Risk, Trading, Sales, or Front Office users.

- Strong understanding of production controls, change management, incident management, release governance, and operational risk reduction.

- Experience with analytics and reporting platforms such as Tableau, Power BI, or similar BI tools.

- Strong technical background, including experience with Python, Bash scripts, SQL, databases, data platforms, application architecture, and modern software delivery practices.

- Ability to influence senior stakeholders and technology teams to align on strategy, priorities, and execution.

- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technology and risk issues to senior management.

- Degree in Computer Science, Finance, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with VaR, Stress Testing, FRTB Aggregation, LMS, Tableau, and Power BI.

- Knowledge of Python, Java, Linux, databases, infrastructure, networking, and cloud or distributed architecture.

jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 276530

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Managing Director, Strategy & Transformation provides strategic direction, transformation leadership, executive advisory support and oversight for the Strategy & Transformation function. This role is accountable for shaping and advancing business-critical priorities, strengthening executive decision-making, enabling disciplined transformation execution, and ensuring strategic initiatives are aligned to financial, client, employee, risk and operational outcomes.

The Managing Director operates as a senior partner to the EVP business heads and key enterprise partners, translating Wealth Management priorities into integrated plans, governance routines, insights and measurable outcomes. The role leads a multi-disciplinary team responsible for strategic projects, executive reporting, employee engagement, client insights and change enablement, while ensuring activities are conducted in compliance with governing regulations, internal policies and procedures.

Is this role right for you? In this role you will:

- Lead and drives a customer focused culture throughout their team to deepen client relationships and leverage broader Bank relationships, systems and knowledge.

- Function as a strategic advisor and trusted partner to the EVP and business heads, providing insight, challenge and recommendations on business strategy, organizational priorities, performance, client outcomes and transformation initiatives to support executive decision-making.

- Shape and leads the enterprise-wide CWM strategy, governance framework and operating cadence translating Canadian Wealth Management and Global Wealth Management priorities into integrated, multi-execution roadmaps with clear accountability, disciplined execution and measurable business outcomes

- Lead the identification, prioritization and execution oversight of enterprise and business-critical initiatives, assessing strategic trade-offs, resource implications, stakeholder impacts and organizational readiness to advance key business objectives.

- Provide executive oversight of a portfolio of complex, cross-functional initiatives with significant business, client, employee and operational impact, ensuring appropriate governance, risk management, stakeholder alignment and realization of intended outcomes.

- Act as the primary point of integration between Global Wealth Solutions leadership, the Office of the Group Head and enterprise partners to ensure strategic priorities are effectively coordinated, communicated and advanced across the organization.

- Establish executive reporting, performance management and business insight frameworks that provide leadership with actionable intelligence, performance transparency and visibility into progress against strategic priorities.

- Provide strategic oversight of client, employee and business performance insights, including ScotiaPulse results, ensuring findings are translated into actionable strategies that strengthen business performance, employee engagement and client outcomes.

- Shape and advances the Global Wealth Solutions transformation agenda by driving alignment across strategy, communications, change management, culture, inclusion initiatives and organizational effectiveness initiatives to support sustainable business growth and performance.

- Build and sustains influential relationships with senior leaders across Global Wealth Management and enterprise functions, leveraging influence and strategic partnership to achieve outcomes in a highly matrixed environment.

- Lead a function through Director and Senior Manager-level direct reports, with accountability for strategic direction, prioritization, governance, quality of executive deliverables, stakeholder alignment and people leadership across the Strategy & Transformation mandate.

- Direct day-to-day activities in a manner consistent with the Bank’s risk culture and the relevant risk appetite statement and limits. Communicates the Bank’s risk culture and risk appetite statement throughout their teams.

- Create an environment in which their team pursues effective and efficient operations of their respective areas in accordance with Scotiabank’s Values, its Code of Conduct and the Global Sales Principles, while ensuring the adequacy, adherence to and effectiveness of day-to-day business controls to meet obligations with respect to operational, compliance, AML/ATF/sanctions and conduct risk.

- Build a high performance environment and implements a people strategy that attracts, retains, develops and motivates their team by fostering an inclusive work environment and using a coaching mindset and behaviours; communicating vison/values/business strategy; and, managing succession and development planning for the team.

Education, Professional Experience, Certifications and Skills required:

- Post-secondary degree, preferably in Business Administration

- 10+/12+ years of progressive experience in strategy, business transformation, wealth management, financial services, distribution channel, management consulting, business management or related leadership roles.

- Demonstrated experience advising EVP/SVP-level executives on business strategy, transformation priorities, performance insights, governance and stakeholder alignment.

- Proven ability to lead complex, cross-functional mandates with enterprise dependencies, competing priorities and senior-level decision-making requirements.

- Deep understanding of wealth management business drivers, client experience, employee engagement, risk/control expectations and operating model considerations.

- Experience establishing governance routines, executive reporting frameworks, KPIs and insights that support prioritization, accountability and business performance.

- Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders in a matrixed environment, including business lines, enterprise functions and external partners.

- Strong people leadership experience, including leading through Director/Senior Manager-level roles, building capability, setting strategic direction and managing performance.

- Proven ability to connect strategy to execution through integrated planning, change management, communications and measurement.

- High degree of judgment, discretion and executive presence, with ability to navigate sensitive and confidential business matters

jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 273028

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Global Transaction Banking (GTB) is the payments and transaction engine of Scotiabank. We support Corporate, Commercial, and Small Business clients with effective treasury management solutions coupled with a best-in-class service model, making it easy for clients to do business with us.

As our clients transform their operating models, expand globally and deploy digital capabilities and their cash management needs are evolving too. Boasting a unique global footprint, GTB’s comprehensive suite of innovative banking solutions help our business clients generate operational efficiencies, streamline treasury processes, simplify payments, improve working capital performance, and mitigate financial risk.

At Scotiabank, we embrace your strengths, ideas, and ambitions. GTB is a fast-growing team with a focus on the Americas, particularly Canada, the U.S., Mexico, and we are seeking top tier talent to complement our organization.

Join a purpose-driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Purpose
The Director, Revenue Management will work to identify and develop strategies that help drive growth and improvement across Global Transaction Banking (GTB) Products. This includes the design and review of financial models that analyze risks, costs, budgets, and overall financial implications of key initiatives. Ensures that the business is achieving maximum results while leveraging efficiencies across products portfolio. Takes ownership of pricing adjudication for business customers on cash management products and operating deposits

What You'll Do:

Strategic Pricing and Revenue Optimization

- Lead the development and execution of strategic pricing, repricing, and revenue optimization initiatives across the GTB product portfolio.

- Develop and implement pricing strategies that balance revenue growth, profitability, competitiveness, and client value.

- Analyze pricing performance, client behavior, industry trends, and competitive positioning to identify commercial opportunities and pricing actions.

- Establish customer segmentation, pricing frameworks, and governance processes that support differentiated value-based pricing strategies.

- Partner with Product, Sales, Finance, Risk, and Operations teams to evaluate, prioritize, and implement pricing decisions.

- Develop business cases, financial models, and impact assessments to support pricing strategy recommendations and investment decisions.

- Monitor pricing performance through key metrics and reporting, providing recommendations to improve commercial outcomes and portfolio profitability.

- Oversee pricing adjudication and governance activities across Business Banking, Commercial Banking, Corporate Banking, Cash Management, Payments, Commercial Cards, and related solutions.

- Ensure pricing decisions appropriately consider client value, market conditions, product utilization, delivery channels, risk, and strategic growth objectives.

Billing & Pricing Transformation

- Lead the strategic transformation of billing and monetization capabilities to support growth, scalability, and enhanced client experience.

- Define and execute the target-state billing operating model, including technology, data, processes, controls, governance, and performance measurement.

- Drive modernization of billing infrastructure and capabilities to support product innovation, commercialization, and revenue growth.

- Establish enterprise billing standards, controls, and best practices that improve transparency, accuracy, and financial discipline while reducing revenue leakage.

- Partner with Technology, Operations, Product, Finance, and Sales teams to simplify and automate billing processes and workflows.

- Champion digitization and automation initiatives that create an efficient, scalable, and client-centric billing ecosystem.

- Deliver data-driven insights and recommendations on billing performance, transformation priorities, and operational effectiveness.

- Identify and implement opportunities to improve billing, pricing, and revenue management processes through continuous improvement and change management initiatives.

- Lead financial planning activities, including product forecasts, business performance reporting, and articulation of key financial drivers.

- Develop risk-reward strategies that optimize portfolio profitability while maintaining alignment with the Bank's risk appetite.

- Build business cases and investment proposals to support strategic initiatives, commercialization efforts, and prioritization decisions.

- Develop market, client, and competitive intelligence to inform product strategies, growth opportunities, and go-to-market plans.

- Conduct scenario analysis and financial modeling to evaluate strategic initiatives, business development opportunities, and portfolio optimization decisions.

- Maintain and enhance key performance metrics, dashboards, and benchmarking frameworks to measure business performance and identify improvement opportunities.

- Support strategic sales initiatives, including RFP responses, pricing proposals, and client solutions that maximize revenue opportunities.

- Lead analytical workstreams and strategic projects, providing actionable insights, recommendations, and execution support for key business priorities.

- Partner with internal and external stakeholders to leverage data, analytics, and market insights that advance GTB strategic objectives.

Risk, Leadership & People Management

- Foster a high-performance, inclusive culture that attracts, develops, and retains top talent through coaching, succession planning, and employee development.

- Promote effective risk management practices by ensuring business decisions align with the Bank's risk appetite, risk culture, and regulatory obligations.

- Maintain strong governance and control frameworks to manage operational, compliance, AML/ATF, conduct, and reputational risks.

- Ensure effective execution of business controls, processes, and oversight activities in accordance with enterprise risk management frameworks and policies.

- Lead organizational change initiatives and stakeholder engagement activities to support strategic transformation and business objectives.

- Undergraduate degree (or equivalent diploma) required; graduate degree an asset; specialization in Finance, Strategy, Analytics, Business, or Marketing

- Understanding of GTB Products financials and P&L levers

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Join Scotiabank at a pivotal time of transformation, where Procurement is driving strategic value and innovation. As the Bank accelerates its adoption of AI and digital capabilities, you’ll play a key role in shaping the future of sourcing within a global organization.

The Role

Help Scotiabank source the technologies shaping the future of banking.

Scotiabank's Procurement function is at a pivotal moment – driving strategic value, commercial discipline, and innovation as the Bank accelerates its digital and AI transformation. As Senior Manager, Strategic Sourcing – covering business line software (e.g., Capital Markets & Wealth Systems) within Technology Sourcing – you'll lead high-impact sourcing strategies across some of the Bank's most complex and fastest-evolving technology domains.

You'll partner with Technology, Risk, Legal, Finance, and senior business leaders to unlock enterprise value across SaaS, cloud & hyperscalers, infrastructure, software, networks. This is a role for a commercially sharp procurement leader who thrives on solving complex problems, influencing spend decisions, and delivering measurable outcomes beyond savings.

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Associate, Corporate Finance Advisory, Investment Banking

Global Banking and Markets
Global Banking and Markets (GBM) is a leading Capital Markets and Investment Banking platform with a  competitive presence across the Americas, operating globally over 100 years. Scotiabank’s strong US presence provides our clients an important bridge to this key global market for trade and investment flows across the Americas and the world.

Global Banking & Markets provides a full range of investment banking, credit and risk management products and services relevant to the financing and strategic development needs of our clients. Our products include debt and equity financing, mergers & acquisitions, corporate banking, institutional equity sales, trading and research, fixed income products, derivatives, energy, foreign exchange and precious metals. We also cross-sell the full range of wholesale products and services offered by the Scotiabank Group including transaction banking and trade finance solutions.

Be part of an innovative Global Capital Markets and Investment Banking business with a unique geographic footprint that puts capital to work for our clients across industries! We work together to drive ambition to every future!

Function Overview
Scotiabank’s Corporate Finance Advisory team sits at the intersection of banking and capital markets. Our team advises corporate clients on capital structure, financing strategy, and credit positioning, as well as strategic decisions across valuation, M&A, shareholder dynamics, and thematic market and sector trends. We partner across the full GBM platform to deliver analytically driven recommendations and differentiated insights that create value for our clients. Core areas of focus include: capital structure optimization, credit analysis, valuation, capital allocation, risk management, and shareholder positioning.

Position Highlights
We are looking for a quantitative associate to lead the delivery of analytical, data-driven content and strategic financial advisory across a diverse range of clients and transactions. This role involves developing financial models and presentations to evaluate market opportunities, weigh capital structure alternatives, assess credit and liquidity needs, and analyze valuation and capital allocation decisions. Working closely with senior bankers, this analyst will translate detailed financial analysis into clear, actionable insights to inform client decisions across capital raising and deployment, M&A, and shareholder strategy. In addition, this role will leverage data science to analyze thematic trends and generate forward-looking perspectives that support client dialogue and origination opportunities.

What You’ll Do

- Evaluate the strategic and financial needs of corporate clients and develop tailored solutions to address them

- Synthesize company, industry, and market data to generate differentiated ideas and identify new business opportunities

- Apply both equity and credit perspectives to provide thoughtful, balanced recommendations and inform due diligence

- Work closely with an analyst team to deliver consistent, high-quality work with strong attention to detail

- Build long-term relationships with clients and collaborate across stakeholders throughout the banking and capital markets platform

- Support deal sourcing and execution through rigorous fundamental analysis, capital markets insights, scenario modeling, and client-ready presentation materials

What You'll Bring:

- A positive, proactive, and intellectually curious mindset required

- MBA, Masters, or PhD degree in a quantitative field preferred

- Bachelor degree also considered if substantial prior experience in investment banking, capital markets, rating agencies, consulting, or equity / credit research

- Professional designations such as CFA, CPA, etc. are a plus

- Proven record of outstanding academic and extracurricular achievement

Work Arrangement:
This position is an on-site role, with the expectation that you will work 5 days a week in the office. Please note that this is subject to change based on the needs of the business.

What You’ll Do

-
Maintains the U.S. Cyber and IT Risk Management Framework and best practices within the Bank while acting as a center of excellence for IT and Cyber Risk in the U.S.

-
Collaborates with the lines of business by acting in a consultative capacity to advise on IT risks that influence their business and ability to meet established strategic objectives, while maintaining oversight and objective challenge.

-
Challenges the IT Risk components of the first line in the Risk & Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) process for the U.S., covering Legal Entities, Processes and Business Lines.

-
Challenges investigation of IT Incidents to define root causes and provides input into remediation actions.

-
Performs Deep Dives and Independent Reviews to assess the effectiveness of controls surrounding key processes, and to identify remediation for gaps to actively and demonstrably mitigate IT and Cybersecurity risks.

-
Challenges IT and Cybersecurity risks within scenario analysis.

-
Monitors Cybersecurity risks and the controls in place within the bank, as well as external Cyber security reporting which may impact the bank.

-
Monitors compliance with IT Risk Policies, Standards and Guidelines.

-
Prepares monthly and quarterly IT and Cyber Risk reporting for U.S. committees and senior management

-
Has good knowledge of risk management practices required to create a culture of risk management compliance.

-
Identifies, assesses, and monitors IT and Cybersecurity related risks based on risk management policies and procedures.

-
Reviews and challenges work of first line of defense for risk management purposes.

-
Exhibits best practice risk management skills through effective internal risk controls, risk monitoring, risk assessment and improvement of risk management processes.

-
Understands how the Bank’s risk appetite and risk culture should be considered in day-to-day activities and decisions.

-
Actively pursues effective and efficient operations of his/her respective areas in accordance with Scotiabank’s Values, its Code of Conduct and the Global Sales Principles, while ensuring the adequacy, adherence to and effectiveness of day-to-day business controls to meet obligations with respect to operational, compliance, AML/ATF/sanctions and conduct risk.

-
Champions a high-performance environment and contributes to an inclusive work environment.

What You’ll Bring

- Strong understanding of IT risk management frameworks in a global banking environment.

- Able to convey complex concepts and ideas on issues requiring interpretation and opinion.

- Independent in judgment and with a high standard of conduct and ethics. Able to challenge and be challenged while maintaining the highest levels of professionalism.

- Good negotiation skills and ability to resolve conflict between teams or individuals so that functional / organizational objectives are achieved.

- Excellent analytical skills; critical thinking and problem solving skills.

- Strong oral and written skills on a business level in English, good presentation skills, and an ability to work with all levels of the organization.

- Good interpersonal skills

- Strong expertise in IT Risk Management (e.g. Logical Access, Data Leakage, Disaster Recovery)

- Experience with Cybersecurity Risk Management is preferred

- A minimum of 7 years of experience in technology departments and/or risk management, preferably in a financial institution

- Industry certifications desirable (e.g., ISACA CRISC)

- Advanced knowledge of relevant regulatory rules (FFIEC, NYDFS 500) and frameworks (NIST, COBIT) is preferred
